title: Diabetes and Instagram: Analysis of Information in Brazilian Publications
screen_reason: QUALITY-ONLY study. The only quantified share of the ~300 Brazilian Instagram posts about pharmacological treatment of diabetes is a DISCERN score band - 'the quality of the information was classified as very poor in 68.8% of the publications'. DISCERN rates the reliability/completeness of treatment information (sources, balance, discussion of risks), not the truth or falsity of what is claimed, so a wholly accurate post can be scored 'very poor'; section 3 of the instructions puts DISCERN squarely in construct QUALITY, and section 1 excludes quality-only studies. The abstract does say the type of information was 'classified as information disorder' and that indication, forms of administration and non-pharmacological treatment 'presented misinformation and/or disinformation', but it attaches NO share and NO denominator to any of that, so there is no extractable CONTENT estimate. The remaining percentages (46.3% mentioning type 2 DM, metformin 10.3%, NPH insulin 7%) are topic-coverage figures, not falsity figures.
missed_or_uncertain: ADJUDICATOR - two things worth a second look. (1) If the review's convention is to record QUALITY rows for the appendix rather than drop the paper (section 3 says a QUALITY row is 'kept, excluded from prevalence', while section 1 says quality-only studies are EXCLUDE-d), then the row to add, verbatim, is: 'The quality of the information was classified as very poor in 68.8% of the publications' - construct QUALITY, Brazil, Instagram, ~300 publications collected 2021-2022, DISCERN Questionnaire, researcher_coding with an inter-examiner kappa reported but not quantified in the abstract, topic health_other (diabetes pharmacotherapy), denom_scope topical, denom_selection curated, unit item, breadth '' (QUALITY). I did not create it because I read section 1's 'QUALITY-ONLY studies' exclusion as governing at the paper level and section 5 as requiring an empty estimates list on EXCLUDE. Everything needed to promote it is in this note. (2) This is an ABSTRACT-ONLY record. The abstract explicitly says a content evaluation was applied 'to categories not included in the quality tool' and that 'the type of information presented was classified as information disorder' - so the full text very probably contains a table giving the share of publications carrying misinformation/disinformation, which would make the paper INCLUDE-able as CONTENT. This paper is a strong candidate for full-text retrieval before the screen is finalised. Also unresolved from the abstract: the exact N ('data from around 300 publications'), the kappa value, and who did the coding.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis of around 300 Brazilian Instagram publications about pharmacological treatment of diabetes mellitus, collected between 2021 and 2022. Instruments: the DISCERN Questionnaire for information quality plus a bespoke content evaluation for categories DISCERN does not cover, with the type of information classified as 'information disorder'. Descriptive statistics; inter-examiner agreement calculated with the kappa coefficient but the value is not given in the abstract. Sampling procedure (how the ~300 posts were found and selected), the exact N, the coders' identity and number, and any external ground truth for accuracy are all unreported in the abstract - full text not available.
rob.item6_quote: The type of information presented was classified as information disorder.
rob.item10_quote: The quality of the information was classified as very poor in 68.8% of the publications.
